messages:
maria: Heads-up — saw a ~4x p99 spike across a subset of requests during a rolling node replace at ~09:12 UTC. Looks tied to autoscale + kernel selection + KV cache cold misses. Opening thread to correlate logs and decide short/long fixes. :warning:
ashwin: Got it. Which model / seq len distribution? Any repro yet?
ryan: Model: text-llama-13b-v1 (non-redwood). Affected requests clustered at seq lengths ~256-768. p50 unchanged, p95 up ~2x, p99 jumped from ~120ms -> ~580ms. No full outage.
jia: Attaching profiler sample (trimmed):
```
2026-03-12 09:12:18.432 profiler: kernel_selector: choose candidate=[fused_attn_sm80, ref_attn] selected=ref_attn reason="kernel unavailable for sm80_frag"
2026-03-12 09:12:18.433 batcher: batch_id=482 size=16 latency_ms=312
2026-03-12 09:12:18.435 kvcache: hit_rate=0.28 -> 0.02 after node-replace
```
maria: That kernel_selector line is interesting — we rolled out a kernel pack yesterday to some regions. Could it be missing symbols on replaced nodes?
infra-bot: [node-manager] replaced node i-0b7c... in pool-rt-eu-west-1 as part of rolling-os-update. replacement_ts=2026-03-12T09:11:54Z
ashwin: If the new node doesn't have the optimized fused kernels, selector falls back to ref_attn which is slower and not batched-friendly. Combined with KV cache misses (different node affinity / IP), we get worse batching and longer latencies.
emanuel: Quick mitigation: pin routing to nodes with the optimized kernels for the canary until we confirm installs. Also bump warm-pool for that zone to avoid routing to fresh nodes during burst.
ryan: I see evidence of affinity churn in request logs: client-route tokens show 30% of in-flight requests switched host mid-session during the replace window. That explains KV cache hit drop.
jia: Small repro script to mimic behavior (runs locally against staging):
```bash
# hammer 50 concurrent sessions with repeated short-context + burst long-context
for i in {1..50}; do curl -sS -X POST $API/run -d '{"model":"text-llama-13b-v1","input_len":512}' & done
```
ashwin: For short term: 1) increase warm-pool size by +2 in eu-west-1 2) extend scale-up cooldown to 45s to avoid rapid churning 3) pin traffic away from nodes lacking kernel pack. Can ops do (1)-(3) now?
maria: ops, can you do (1)-(3)? We'll monitor p99 for 15m.
infra-bot: Warm pool increased: pool-rt-eu-west-1 -> desired=6 (+2) by ops-user. Routing pin applied to nodes with tag=kernel-pack:v2. cooldown updated to 45s.
emanuel: Mid-term fix ideas: 1) kernel selector should include a stability score: prefer kernels that have been used successfully on node for N minutes (avoid transient missing-symbol fallbacks). 2) KV cache affinity: soften eviction when host rotates during rolling upgrades (grace window). 3) add per-node kernel health probe during node boot to ensure pack present before routing.
ashwin: Also worth improving batcher heuristics: when kernel fallback occurs for a subset of nodes, reduce cross-node batching for those request classes to avoid stragglers inflating tail.
ryan: Logged a PR with initial telemetry additions: adds "kernel_candidate_history" to trace, and new metric kv_affinity_churn_rate. Link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/834 (canary").
maria: Thanks. Ops reports p99 dropped back to ~140ms 10m after warm-pool bump and pin. Keeping thread open for postmortem notes and timeline. Please paste any additional logs here. :white_check_mark:
